historical_references.reference: Hildegard of Bingen was a German Benedictine abbess, writer, composer, philosopher, Christian mystic, and polymath, born around 1056 in Bingen am Rhein. She is considered one of the most significant figures in medieval Europe for her writings, musical compositions, and her social and political influence. Her writings encompass works on theology, medicine, natural history, and music theory. She is also known for her visions and her foundation of the monastery of Rupertsberg. Hildegard's earliest recorded visions began when she was around three years old, and continued throughout her life.
historical_references.context: Medieval Europe, Benedictine abbess, writer, composer, philosopher, Christian mystic, polymath, visions, monastery of Rupertsberg

historical_references.reference: Saint Hildegard of Bingen, or Sibylle of the Rhine, was a German visionary, writer, composer, and Abbess who founded the Monastery of Sainte-Disibode in Disibodenberg, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. She is considered one of the first European women known to have composed liturgical music. In 1098, at the age of 42, she founded the monastery of Rupertsberg for women, and in 1100, she was appointed abbess. She is also known for her writings on medicine and natural history, as well as her visions and prophecies.
